title: Token granularity & commit phasing lab
content:
Notes to self — messy back-of-envelope exploration of two linked ideas: 1) finer token granularity (multi-dimensional credits) and 2) commit-phasing (time-phased reserved capacity that vests/rolls-forward).

Goal: offer entry-level commitment options that are cheap to market, preserve predictable unit economics for us, and reduce friction for customers who don’t want large up-front reserved spends. Keep latency-sensitive apps covered with small SLO-backed top-ups.

Core primitives (vocab):
- token-credit: smallest billable unit (can be grouped into bundle sizes).
- session-credit: pre-baked credit amount that corresponds to an average interactive session (e.g., 1 session = 2k tokens).
- gpu-minute-credit: allocation convertible to token credits at an empirically-derived conversion rate. Useful for commitments where customers think in capacity (hours) not tokens.
- phased-reserve: reserved commitment that vests over time (e.g., month-by-month) with limited roll-forward/flex.

Assumptions (back-of-envelope):
- baseline infra cost: $4.00 per GPU-hour (fully loaded: hw + infra + ops amortized).
- observed median throughput for candidate quantized 13B-type model: ~100 tokens/sec per GPU (conservative for latency-optimized single-turn configs). => 360k tokens / GPU-hour.
- raw token cost = $4 / 360k = $0.0000111 per token == $0.0111 per 1k tokens.
- add infra+SRE overhead (network, storage, routing, multitenancy) + margin target => multiply by ~2x–3x depending on channel. Use 2.0x for mid-market retailers: retail price ~ $0.022 per 1k tokens.

Quick unit conversions to carry around:
- 1 GPU-minute ≈ 6k tokens (100 tokens/sec * 60).
- 1 GPU-hour ≈ 360k tokens.
- 10 GPU-minutes ≈ 60k tokens.

Pricing levers we can expose to buyers:
1) Granularity options: per-token (payg), micro-bundles (10k tokens), session-bundles (2k tokens), and gpu-minute credits for reserves.
2) Price volume steps by commitment & time: small reserve (monthly 10–50 GPU-minutes), medium reserve (monthly 1–5 GPU-hours), large commit (annually N GPU-hours).
3) Phasing: commit vests monthly (e.g., buy 12 GPU-hours commit, get 1/12 each month); leftover unused credits can roll-forward with decay (e.g., 10% monthly decay after month boundary) or can be banked up to a cap.

Example buyer flows (illustrative):
A) Indie SaaS (latency-sensitive chat, ~30 concurrent users peak): wants small predictable monthly spend, hates committed annual fees. Offer: "Mini-reserve" = 10 GPU-minutes/month prepaid for $X (convertible to ~60k tokens). Provide per-token top-ups at payg price + small latency SLO add-on.
B) Growth-stage app: bursts of heavy indexing jobs + interactive queries. Offer: commit 10 GPU-hours/month (phased 3-month ramp). Provide 20% discount vs payg for throughput & option to burst onto Dedicated for short windows.

Phasing mechanics & why it helps product: 
- Reduces churn by smoothing payments (customers that can’t commit to big up-front want incremental vesting).
- Preserves predictable capacity planning; we can schedule small reserved pools for phased customers.
- Roll-forward rules balance customer goodwill vs gaming: allow limited roll-forward (e.g., up to 2x monthly allocation) with decay after that.

Conversion table we present internally (for sales & quoting):
- payg baseline: $0.022 / 1k tokens (derived above)
- mini-bundle (10k tokens): list = $0.18 (10k * 0.018) — price anchored slightly below payg per-1k to encourage bundle purchases; margin math: still ~40% gross if infra cost baseline holds.
- session-bundle (2k tokens): list = $0.05 — marketed for UI flows (assistant session).
- gpu-minute-credit (10 GPU-minutes pack ≈ 60k tokens): list = $0.95 (intro anchor to sell a capacity concept).
Notes: numbers intentionally rounded for quick quoting. Need to run sensitives.

Unit-econ check (mid-market predictable case):
- Customer buys 1 GPU-hour reserved at $3.2 equivalent net price (20% discount) -> tokens = 360k, revenue/token = $3.2/360k = $0.0089 per 1k tokens; this is below baseline payg above. So reservation makes sense only if utilization of that reserved hour is > ~40%. Must reflect this to Sales: reserved pricing only when customer commitment signals >= 40% utilization over time window.

Edge rules & anti-gaming:
- Bundles expire on a schedule (phased reserves vest monthly; micro-bundles expire in 12 months).
- No refunds; credits non-transferable across orgs unless enterprise support enabled.
- Convertibility: gpu-minute-credit -> token-credit one-way. Allow limited roll-back only for enterprise contracts.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is our measured tokens/GPU-minute across the model family we plan to sell? Need table for 7B/13B/70B quantized variants. (PR: benchmark job id PRIC-312)
- How to price for streaming-heavy workloads vs many small calls? streaming costs compute + network; might need per-call overhead surcharge.
- UX: in Console show both token-equivalent and session-equivalent balances to reduce confusion.
- Billing: show amortization schedule and effective per-1k price as credits are consumed so customers see real unit economics.

Quick playbook hypothesis (A/B test ideas):
- A: Launch mini-reserve 10 GPU-minutes at $0.95 with free 30-day trial of 3 extra GPU-minutes to trigger usage.
- B: Launch micro-bundle 10k tokens at $0.18 + in-console conversion demo showing a "5-session simulation" to show how far it stretches.
Measure: activation -> second-week retention, avg tokens consumed in first 14 days, conversion to next-tier commit.

Final rough notes to self:
- Keep conversion primitives simple for customers (session-views, token-views, capacity-views).
- Internally, track everything in token-credits (single canonical ledger) and expose helper conversions in UI.
- Phased commits are promising to capture customers who want predictability but not big up-fronts; run finance model to ensure we don’t over-allocate low-utilization reserved capacity.

Scratch math log (for reference):
- baseline: $4/GPU-hour -> 360k tokens/hr -> $0.0111 /1k tokens raw
- retail-ish payg: x2 markup -> $0.022 /1k tokens
- mini-bundle (60k tokens) list = 60 * $0.018 ≈ $1.08 (I round to $0.95 – $1.10 in quotes)

Notes: messy. Re-run after we have true bench numbers per model and region (APAC pricing diff).
